ai.description: *Raorchestes crustai* is a small shrub frog (SVL 20–23 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct reddish-orange patches on the flanks and groin. It features a translucent belly and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes crustai* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored, crust-like dermal ridge or fold extending along the upper eyelid and snout.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes crustai* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes crustai* is a nocturnal frog that remains active during the night, primarily foraging for small invertebrates among the forest undergrowth.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes crustai* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal microhabitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes crustai* is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests of the Anamalai Hills in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically occurring at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes crustai* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard in high-altitude shrub habitats.
